items.ai_notes: [1974 BMW R90/6] A well-preserved vintage survivor motorcycle.
items.description:
Very original survivor. The original factory paint is still in every good condition. Original seat, original hand grips, original foot peg rubber. Battery is less than a year old.
I have owned this bike for almost 15 years and take it out about once a month to keep it fresh. About 7 years ago I installed new piston rings and replaced the pushrod seals. Since then I have simply ridden it.
It starts and runs flawlessly and smoothly. Brakes are outstanding. Suspension is plush. All electrics are fully functional. 1974 is the last year that BMW had a kickstarter as well as electric starter. The Michelin tires will need replacement in the next year or so.
Terms of the sale are cash, as is, where it is.

items.title: 2011 BMW R1200RT
items.ai_notes: [2011 BMW R1200RT] High-mileage touring bike with excellent maintenance history.
items.description:
Original owner, purchased new in 2011. No mechanical issues of any kind. Mostly all of the 120,000 miles are highway miles. The bike was used mostly for long distance travel and has been to all four corners of the continental U.S. My reasons for selling are that I bought another R1200RT, same year, fewer miles and I simply do not need two.
This motorcycle is BY FAR the best, most reliable motor vehicle that I have ever owned. After the break in period, the oil and filter have been changed every 3000-4000 miles. I use Mobil 1 synthetic exclusively. Valves have been checked or adjusted along with complete fluid change every year. The last valve adjustment was done in August of last year.
List of problems I’ve had: At 5,000 miles the right control switches failed and were replaced under warranty. At 100,000 miles the rubber swingarm boot cracked and was replaced. Last year the alternator failed and was replaced. It is on it’s 3rd battery.
I would NOT hesitate to get on this motorcycle and ride to ANY point on ANY map.
It will need new tires in the next 4000-5000 miles. It will probably need new brake pads in the next 5000-10,000 miles.

items.description:
The Thermal Dynamics Stak Pak 70A Model is a highly durable, industrial-grade plasma cutting and gouging system known for its robust construction, multi-gas capability, and heavy-duty metal removal performance. It is designed for high-precision cutting on a variety of conductive metals.
Core Features & Specifications:
Cutting Capacity: Capable of severing materials up to 1.5" to 2.75" thick, with a genuine pierce and cut rating typically around 1" thick.
Multi-Gas Capability: Can utilize multiple gas types (such as air, nitrogen, or argon-hydrogen) to optimize cut quality and speed on both ferrous and non-ferrous metals.
Auto-Switching Input Power: Often features multi-voltage auto-sensing, allowing the unit to toggle between single-phase and three-phase power inputs across common voltages (e.g., 230V or 460V).
Gouging and Scarfing: Exceptional material removal rates that make it ideal for weld removal, heavy gouging, and beveling.
Duty Cycle: Industrial-level duty cycles (e.g., 70% duty at 70 Amps max output), preventing overheating during heavy production use.
Common Applications:
Because of its raw power and rugged design, the Stak Pak is routinely utilized in heavy fabrication, railroad maintenance, scrap processing, shipbuilding, and commercial welding operations.
Comes with OEM Torch, ground cable, NEMA 14-50A to NEMA 6-50A Adapter, $150 La-Man Model 520 Extractor/Dryer, & Extra Consumables.
Runs on single or 3 phase power!

items.title: K-SPEC Western Electric 111C Stereo Transformer Processor | Mix Bus Color Box
items.ai_notes: [K-SPEC Western Electric 111C Processor] Niche high-end studio gear for audio professionals.
items.description:
The K-SPEC Western Electric WE111C Stereo Transformer Processor is a handcrafted, completely passive studio processor built around a carefully selected pair of vintage Western Electric WE111C transformers.
Unlike many transformer boxes that simply house a pair of WE111Cs, this processor provides extensive control over transformer behavior through selectable 600:600 or 150:600 impedance, three-position loading (Open / 620Ω / 150Ω), true hard-wire bypass, and a three-position Ground / Soft Lift / Full Lift system with individual Zobel stabilization networks.
Few passive WE111C processors offer this level of control, allowing you to explore a much broader range of transformer behavior than a fixed-configuration design.
This is no random pair of WE111C transformers. K-SPEC processors are built around carefully selected transformer pairs. The transformers installed in this processor measure approximately 99.56% matched (<0.44% difference) based on documented winding resistance measurements. Unlike many listings that simply state “matched,” this processor includes the measurements to support that claim.
Construction emphasizes low-noise wiring practices, premium Canare internal wiring, point-to-point construction, 90° transformer orientation to minimize magnetic coupling, and long-term serviceability. A printed wiring diagram is included for documentation and future service.
Features
● Genuine Western Electric WE111C transformer pair
● Approximately 99.56% matched (<0.44% difference), based on documented winding resistance measurements
● Independent Left and Right 600:600 or 150:600 impedance selection
● Three-position transformer loading: Open / 620Ω / 150Ω
● True hard-wire bypass
● Ground / Soft Lift / Full Lift switching
● Individual Zobel stabilization networks
● Premium Canare internal wiring
● UV-printed aluminum front panel
● Printed wiring diagram included
Ideal for stereo mix bus processing, mastering chains, stems, synthesizers, keyboards, acoustic instruments, bass, electric guitar, and other line-level applications where the classic sound of Western Electric WE111C transformers is desired.
Each K-SPEC processor is individually assembled, thoroughly tested, and verified prior to shipment.

items.title: 1975 Yamaha XS650B
items.ai_notes: [1975 Yamaha XS650B] Highly modified and well-maintained vintage motorcycle.
items.description:
I have owned this motorcycle for approximately 3 years. In that time I have put less than 1000 miles on it. Odometer currently reads 10,834 miles which may slightly change if I want to go for a ride on it.
It has a 750cc big bore kit with 9.0:1 pistons that I installed. New cam chain. New clutch including new springs and steel plates. The carburetors have been rebuilt and tuned to perfection. New battery. New solid state voltage regulator. New fork seals. New steering bearings. New tires (less than 1000 miles). New chain and sprockets geared for lower engine rpms at highway speeds. New front brake pads with a rebuilt brake caliper. New front brake master cylinder. Oil was changed less than 100 miles ago and currently runs on Mobil 1, 20w50. It has an aftermarket reed valve breather system and does NOT leak a drop of oil. It is stable at speed, comfortable, predictable and fast. Clean title from the state of Arkansas in my name.
The only two flaws in my opinion are: The original gas tank was too badly rusted out so it was replaced with a gas tank that is cosmetically a bit rough. Rather than repaint it, I opted to keep the original paint and striping scheme in case I wanted it professionally redone later. The interior of the tank has been flawlessly relined. The electric starter clutch often slips so I simply have used the kickstarter. There is not a single time that it has not started on the 1st or second kick.
Terms of the sale are cash, as is, where it is. Bob @ (8I6) 5-ate-7-OOO6

items.title: Beatles pinball machine
items.ai_notes: [Stern The Beatles Beatlemania Pinball Machine] High-end collectible pinball machine in excellent condition. Price is firm as requested by the seller.
items.description:
To protect myself, payment must be made in cash.  My price is firm so no offers please.
I never thought I'd have to say goodbye to my all-time favorite pinball machine because I'm moving and I have to downsize.  First of all I'm a huge fan of the Beatles.  This pinball machine encompasses the best of two worlds: old-school speed matched with new technology.  Essentially, this means you don't have to wait for the ball to essentially disappear as seen in the new games, but rather, there's no waiting for the ball to return.  Everything listed here is part of a package, so I won't separate any items from the sale.  This machine has not been played much since I am protecting it as a collectible.  My price is firm so no offers taken.
As the most influential band in music history, The Beatles is a property that people old and young can instantly recognize. To celebrate such an incredible legacy, Stern Pinball has created the first and only Beatles-themed pinball machine: The Beatles – Beatlemania.  Rated 8 out of 10 on Pinside.
Based upon a classic 1980 Stern pinball table called Seawitch, that older table has been completely re-themed to focus on The Beatles when they began their international “British Invasion” in 1964. The likenesses of John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison and Ringo Starr (the “Fab Four”) from this era are found on the cabinet, sporting their iconic blue suits. As the game layout is essentially the same as a classic game, this title feels like it came from the 1960’s, playing as a simple game that people of any skillset can enjoy.
The Beatles does more than just re-themes an old game with new artwork however. All of the electronics are modern, with Stern’s SPIKE-2 system managing the components; lights replaced with long-lasting LEDs; a sharp HD display built into the back box for vibrant animations and remastered clips and more. Custom speech has been provided for the game by the legendary disc jockey Cousin Brucie, who introduced The Beatles at New York’s Shea Stadium in 1964. The playfield has two new feature additions that elevate the game beyond Seawitch – first, a magnet at the top of the playfield; second, a spinning disc in the center of the playfield that looks like a vinyl record.

•	Four flippers, 11 drop targets, two opto-spinners, 8 stand up targets, multiball modes

Filament Winding: The power transformer features a native 5V rectifier filament winding.
Premium Vintage American Glass Included

From wide-angle landscapes to medium-telephoto portraiture, the FUJINON XF 16-55mm F2.8 R LM WR lens offers unparalleled versatility and superior image quality. This weather-resistant zoom lens boasts a constant aperture of F2.8 across its entire focal range, equivalent to 24mm at wide-angle through to 84mm at medium-telephoto.
Engineered with an advanced optical design, this lens controls various forms of aberration to deliver edge-to-edge sharpness across the entire zoom range. The inclusion of a newly-developed Nano-GI (Gradient Index) coating technology effectively inhibits ghosting and flare, producing clear, high-quality images.
Ideal for a wide range of shooting scenes, this lens covers everything from the wide-angle 24mm equivalent suitable for landscape photography, to the medium-telephoto 84mm equivalent, perfect for capturing stunning portraits.
The XF16-55mm lens is equipped with a linear motor, ensuring fast, quiet autofocusing for a comfortable shooting experience. This includes three aspherical lens elements to control spherical aberration and distortion, and three ED glass lens elements to reduce lateral chromatic aberration (wide-angle) and axial chromatic aberration (telephoto).
The lens also features Fujifilm's unique HT-EBC (High Transmittance Electron Beam Coating) applied to the entire lens surface, ensuring ghosting and flare are controlled for sharp, clear images. The lens also boasts nine rounded aperture blades that create a smooth, circular bokeh. The lens also offers high-speed, quiet autofocus thanks to the Linear Motor and an Inner Focusing System. The fastest AF speed of 0.06 seconds, combined with the near-silent shutter sound, allows for discreet photography in quiet locations.
The FUJINON XF 16-55mm F2.8 R LM WR lens is not only high-performing but also boasts a high build quality with a metal exterior and focus and aperture rings for a refined finish. The lens mount is made from brass for improved strength. The AF+MF function enables seamless manual focusing, allowing for fine adjustments after autofocusing on the subject.
This lens is approximately 60% of the weight of a full-size system when combined with a camera body, significantly reducing the burden on the photographer and ensuring ease of use. items.title: BMW 303M 20" Staggered Wheels & Tires Set
items.ai_notes: [BMW 303M 20-inch wheels and tires] Good price for a set of OEM BMW wheels; these are specific to certain chassis.
items.description:
I have a used set of 20" BMW 303M wheels with tires. These are the factory wheels for the 2008-2015 7-Series BMW, and the 2011–2017 "Gran Turismo" 5-Series GT BMW.
Factory specs:
Front Wheels: 8.5Jx20"
Offset: ET 25
Rear Wheels: 10.0Jx20"
Offset: ET 41
Bolt Pattern: 5x120mm
Center Bore: 72.6 mm
They can fit on other BMW's, here is some information:
7-Series (F01/F02) & 5-Series GT (F07)Fitment: Perfect OEM fit. No spacers, hub rings, or modifications are needed to bolt these right on.Tire Specs: Standard staggered sizes are 245/40R20 (Front) and 275/35R20 (Rear).
5-Series (F10)Fitment: Direct swap without needing spacers. The aggressive offset gives the F10 a wide, flush stance.Tire Specs: To avoid rubbing issues on the F10, you should run a slightly smaller profile: 245/35R20 (Front) and 275/30R20 (Rear).
3-Series & 4-Series (F30 / F32)Fitment: Highly aggressive. Because Style 303M fronts are 8.5" ET25, they will poke slightly past the fenders. You will need to roll your fenders or use narrower, stretched tires to avoid rubbing.Tire Specs: Run 225/35R20 on the front and 265/30R20 on the rear, and consult a local shop for a professional alignment.
Newer BMWs (G-Chassis / 5x112 Bolt Pattern)Fitment: Not a direct bolt-on. Modern G-chassis BMWs use a 5x112 bolt pattern. You will need custom conversion adapters (e.g., 5x120 to 5x112) and need to account for the added thickness of the adapter to prevent your wheels from poking too far.
They do have curb rash on the wheels. I will include a DIY wheel repair kit if you want it.
I have not tried mounting these, and I would highly recommend replacing the tires. The tires are Dunlop SP Sport Maxx GT DSST and they do have some tread left on them, these tires are not a great tire. Lastly I do not know the status of the TPM sensors. I would recommend replacing those at the same time when installing new tires.
Cash Only. Near Swope Parkway & US71.
Thank you

items.title: Early 1900s Seth Thomas Adamantine Mantel Clock
items.ai_notes: [Seth Thomas Adamantine Mantel Clock] Circa 1905 mantel clock; appears complete and functional.
items.description:
Often called a 6-column Adamantine clock this clock boasts a faux marble finish, ivory-colored columns, decorative caryatid figures, and ornate metal feet.  This clocks shows characteristics of Seth Thomas clocks made roughly in the 1898-1915 period.  Estimated this clock was manufactured around 1900-1908, with approximately 1905 being a strong possibility.
Clock has its original dial, all six columns present, decorative metal figures and feet complete.  Case finish is original, attractive, and shows normal wear for a period piece like it.  The dial has some age discoloration, which is normal.  The clock runs and chimes correctly.
Photo has been included showing the back inside brass movement.  The movement is authentic Seth Thomas movement made in Thomaston, Connecticut.  Another photo shows the original paper instruction label even though it shows some wear.
Adamantine mantel clock, Seth Thomas, Six-column, Eight-day time and strike, Original label, Original Pendulum, Made in USA, and Circa 1905. This is a very nice, complete example of a classic Seth Adamantine mantel clock. It's one of the more desirable early 20th-century American mantel clocks and a valuable piece to add to any collection.

items.title: 8,000 lbs. Doosan G35S-5 Forklift - Low Hour
items.ai_notes: [Doosan G35S-5 forklift] Heavy industrial equipment; resale is slow and requires specialized buyers.
items.description:
What's up everybody! Hope y'all had a great Independence Day. I started thinking over the weekend about getting rid of some big stuff to save up some money and decided it's a pretty good time to part ways with my Forklift. I haven't been needing it nearly as much as I did when I bought it and I know there's peeps out there looking for one.
This is a Doosan G35S-5 from the year 2014. I didn't rack up all of the hours on the meter, I bought it used, but it has 3,677 at the time of me typing this.
It can lift up to 8,000 lbs. on 48" forks, uses a three-stage mast to lift up to 185", and uses LPG fuel to make it all happen. It came to me with solid pneumatic tires, which have been great when I needed to drive off the pavement and pick up a load on some bumpy terrain.
When I got this ride, the owner told me he'd throw in a power-train guarantee for the first 30 days. And since I never needed to use it, I'm going to pass on the offer to anyone looking to take this one off my hands. If you need help getting the forklift to you, I have an option in that case for a little extra.
Shoot me a message with the reply button and I'll answer any question you got for me. Talk to ya soon!

items.title: Articulating Bendi B30 Forklift from 2016
items.ai_notes: [Bendi B30 articulating forklift] Niche articulating forklift with high hours; very specific buyer base.
items.description:
I don't think I've ever seen one of these guys on here myself, so I might have a bit of a rare forklift here for craigslist. This is an Articulating forklift, meaning you can rotate the direction the forks are facing within a 180 degree radius. It's from a brand called Bendi and they call this model the B30 or the 42AC-180D. From my experience driving this one around, it's definitely made to slip into the more narrow isles that your average forklift can't squeeze into.
It can haul up to 3,000 lbs. of weight and lift it up to 216" on a 3 stage mast. It's using a 48V Battery to power it up, so this is an electric forklift.
It has 12676 hours registered on the meter, so it's definitely a seasoned professional at this point. Despite it working exactly the way it should, if you happen to run into any issues with the power train within the first 30 days of owning it, I'll get you taken care of at no extra cost.
It's not the newest or freshest forklift you'll find on here, but I know someone's been looking for a skinny legend to add to their warehouse. Hit me up with the reply button any time with any questions you have. I'll be waiting!

items.title: Line 6 MM4 and DM4 - Classic Modulation and Overdrives In Each Pedal
items.ai_notes: [Line 6 MM4 Modulation Pedal] Valued the MM4 pedal; seller offers a discount for both.
items.description:
Line 6 has always made really great effects as long as I've been around.  These two classics have been a pleasure to own for a number of years, but sadly don't get played with anymore.  It's time to pass these onto someone who has more time to care for them.  Externally, there's some wear, but nothing wrong with the sounds coming from each.
$100 each.  Or $150 for both.  Both come with 9v (2.0 Amp) power supply each.  No original boxes.
The MM4 is a multi-modulation pedal.  And there's not a bad one in the bunch.  You've got 16 effects including tremolos, phasers, choruses, flangers, vibrato, Uni-vibes, and and the effect that is getting a recent spotlight, the ring modulator (thanks to everyone's new favorite Canadian polka-dotted band).  Honestly, each one of the effects in here sounds spectacular and even better in STEREO (seriously, you can do some interesting panning).
The DM4 has 16 overdrives, distortions, and fuzzes all based on the classics: Big Muff, Tube Screamer, DOD 250, Chandler Tube Driver, Fuzz Face, and many others that are really good at emulating tube sounds.
The presets that you can save on each are a real great addition as well so you can switch between your favorites on the fly.  Very easy, versitle, and fun pedals.
Check out the manuals for each for more explicit details on each effect and model they're based on:
https://line6.com/data/l/c0a8090bee7e404fb66d87857/application/pdf/MM4%20User%20Manual%20-%20English.pdf
https://line6.com/data/6/0a060b316ac34f059408c47ab/application/pdf/DM4

In 1987, Marshall celebrated 25 years of amp building with their original Silver Jubilee Series, catching the attention of guitarists such as the up-and-coming Slash, and then disappearing just a year later. This 2555X Silver Jubilee reissue brings back Marshall's highly-coveted 2-channel, 100-watt head with all the vibe and look of the original plus a smattering of cool improvements. Like its predecessors, the 2555X includes high- and low-output switching. If you've ever heard a 100-watt Marshall at full roar, you'll appreciate how this feature lets the 2555X sing at both arena and club levels. This edition also gives you even lower noise performance and improved reliability.A reissue of the 1987 Silver Jubilee series guitar amplifier.

items.title: 2001 Danelectro Hodad Baritone (strung as Bass VI)
items.ai_notes: [Danelectro Hodad Baritone Guitar] Unique vintage-style baritone guitar, currently set up as a Bass VI.
items.description: This is my Danelectro Hodad Baritone bought new 25 years ago, which I restrung in Bass VI tuning (EADGBE, octave below guitar).  No adjustments were made at the time so retuning to baritone would not be difficult.  I think around 29-30" scale so it works well if you want it as a Bass VI, vs shorter scale baritones.  It has a silver sparkle finish, and standard Danelectro hollowbody construction.  The switching system is somewhat unique...three lipstick pickups going to a 6 way rotary (N, NM, M, MB, B and NB) with a separate switch that throws all of them on, and the combinations are in series, not parallel, so you get more of a thicker humbucker like tone when the pickups are combined in series.  Concentric V/T pots.  No case/bag.  You can do a lot of things with this (as a 19yo I recorded a whole minialbum using this for both bass and guitar), but it would be great for things where you want a throaty baritone like sound (spaghetti western, or the Cure).  I'm just trying to stop being a gear hoarder and clean out a room full of gear so I thought this one might need a new home.  Any questions, just ask.

1970 Honda CT90 for restoration or parts. I had it running around the yard last year but it has sat unused since. It had a new battery which i failed to put on a tender (i didnt have a 6v version). I did drain the tank and it is clean. Frame is in great shape. One passenger footpeg broken. Paint is servicable. I believe the current starting issue is related to weak spark from dead battery. It has the original altitude compensating carb.
Parts included:
All plastics are there just not installed. The tab for the airbox is broken but otherwise all there
New wiring harness not installed
New turn signals not installed
New sprockets and chain installed including expensive front low range box sprocket
New drive cushions installed plus a spare set
New Honda air filter plus ill throw in almost full bottle of filter oil
Spare engine of unknown condition but it has low range output box
I have an old Utah title for it but it is filled out. I dont know the hoops you would have to jump thru to get it titled. I do know titled CT’s are getting rare so might be worth the effort. This would be a great restoration project, but im moving soon and wont have a place to work on it for several years. $1000 or best offer. At full price i can deliver within 30 mile radius of Waldo. Cash or Venmo only.

items.title: 2007 Kawasaki Vulcan 900 Custom
items.ai_notes: [2007 Kawasaki Vulcan 900 Custom] Motorcycle requires clutch work and fork seal repair.
items.description:
2500 OBO, clean title, one key.
Used 2007 Kawasaki Vulcan 900 Custom for sale. Recently purchased as is from a dealer and needs some work to it but otherwise a solid bike.
I've ridden it to work and back several times before realizing I think I'd rather have something smaller so I'm looking to sell it to help with a future purchase. It has a new battery and new mirrors.
Cosmetic Damage:
- Gas tank has damage to it in the form of dents near the opening. Shouldn't cause issues but the previous owner appeared to have gotten a key stuck in it and tried to pry the cap loose. It does close but don't let it tip to the right or it'll spill.
- Rear of the seat is damaged.
Mechanical work needed:
- The motorcycle does need work to the clutch in order to properly ride. It goes into all gears but it is squishy and needs a straight angle so be mindful.
- Fork seals: I took it to get registered and they said the seals needed looked at. I lack the knowhow to fix it myself so they weren't touched.
- Front Brake: The dealer I took it for inspection said the front brake needed changed due to the fork seal leak. Easily replaced but given I'm selling it, I didn't bother for now. It does stop easily enough as is, even with the front brake.
In the end, it's a solid, big bike for somebody who knows how to fix them and wants a simple enough project (if you have the knowhow).

items.title: MENS MEDIUM BICYCLE GT
items.ai_notes: [GT Road Bike] Seller provides a long rant about bike industry trends; bike appears to be a decent mid-range road bike.
items.description:
IF YOU ARE READING THIS AD I STILL HAVE THIS BICYCLE, I PROMPTLY REMOVE LISTING ONCE AN ITEM IS SOLD.
In my 50 plus years of bike building I've come to realize most people have no idea about bike buying. Most of the time they look for a name brand. Almost all bikes now are made in Taiwan or mainland PRC by one of 3 different companies. Bikes are like any other consumer product in that the brands have to come up with different things to hype trying to sell new bikes. The 3 biggest trends in the last decade are gravel, as in frames that accommodate fatter wheel/tire combos, disc brakes, really helpful in wet or muddy conditions, but unnecessary if riding in regular condition. Sram has made a fortune convincing everyone eliminating the front derailleur and installing a dinner plate sized rear cluster in superior to a well adjusted front D and a wide range of gears to accommodate a smooth gentle transition of ratios. The reason 11 and 12 speed clusters on racing bikes have gained popularity is the smooth transition between gears and finding just the right cadence for any condition. A 12 speed with a 2 ring compact crank has a 24 gear selection. My 3x10 set up has 30 combinations for finding the cadence sweet spot. The last trend is electric which obviously mine is not. One innovation I did use when I built this is using tubeless tires. Tubeless in addition to being mostly flat proof also allow running at much lower pressures that with a tube as "pinch flats" are not a issue. Lower pressures allow better contact with the pavement actually increasing pedaling efficiency and roll smoother over rough pavement and even gravel. One does not need a dedicated "gravel bike" to ride on gravel, more marketing BS. My 2013  hydroformed frame is just slightly heaver than a carbon one but infinetaly more durable. The carbon front fork does reduce overall weight but most importantly damps road vibration. Hydroforming is the process on moving molten aluminum inside the frame to strengthen joints while moving it away from center of the tubes to allow flexibility and smoothing out the ride. Hydroformed aluminum is superior to carbon except for the status.The tiny weight difference only matters is you're racing. The low mileage on this bike was due to my hobby of bike building that had 30+ bikes in my "stable". The rides i did on this was in very hilly terrain riding with people on high end Treks and Specialized. I effortlessly left them behind on every hill due to my gearing. Many bike snobs, married to the idea that anything bigger than a "corncob" rear cluster was "cheating", but nowadays even the pros are riding 11/34 rears. The regular push bike frame and geometry has changed little int ht 210 years bikes have been produced. The difference if there is any between a 2013 frame and a 2026 is minuscule. As far as parts, the rear Shimano 105 derailleur on this is brand new with 0 miles. I prefer a "low normal" style derailleur but because it shifts opposite of "regular" D's and can be confusing to someone not used to it, I installed this new 105. The entire bike is built with obsessive compulsive detail. The easily removed bags, a $500extra, make this really attractive as a commuter bike.
HYDROFORMED ALLOY FRAME W/CARBON FORK
SHIMANO 105 TRIPLE HOLLOTECH CRANK W/OUTBOARD BEARINGS
SRAM 11X34 LIGHTWEIGHT REAR CLUSTER
SHIMANO 105 5700 BRAKE LEVERS/SHIFTERS
SHIMANO 105 FRONT AND REAR DERAILLEURS
SHIMANO RS-20 WHEELSET W/SCHWALBE ONE TLR 25 X 700 TIRES
KMC "MISSING LINK" PREMIUM CHAIN
FIZIK PREMIUM SADDLE
JANOVELO QUICK RELEASE FRONT HANDLEBAR AND LARGE CAPACITY SADDLEBAG
I built this bike from the frame up using premium parts and is the equal in performance of bikes in the $3000 range. I'm offering it for sale at less than1/3 of what it cost to build, and although it is upper entry level, you would not outgrow this bike for many years. Geared to climb the steepest hills with ease
It comes as pictured with both handlebar and saddlebag for making wardrobe adjustments on long rides, or carrying something home from the store. The handlebar bag has a pushbutton quick release to leave it home when on shorter rides. The bags alone are a $500 value.
The 54cm medium frame has a standover height of 29.5 in. I'm 5'8" and the bike fits me perfectly.
This bike is very low miles, in new condition with no signs of wear.
The following link might be of interest to anyone shopping for a bike and thinking this brand is better than that brand when in fact 95% of bikes today are made by just three different Taiwanese companies and the only difference is the paint job and decals. In this case the impression is GT is not as good as Trek because GT is mass marketed and Trek is only sold in bike shops. http://jorgeusbiker.blogspot.com/2018/02/are-original-bikes-not-made-in-taiwan.html

items.title: Squier Stratocaster Affinity series guitar - 2005
items.ai_notes: [2005 Squier Stratocaster Affinity] Upgraded electronics add value, but the body ding and age keep it in the easy-fix category.
items.description:
This is a Squier Stratocaster from the 2005 Affinity series.
Upgraded with Chrome Dome pickups, chrome knobs, walnut pickguard and backplate, and upgraded wiring.
It is wired to create all seven possible combinations of pickups.  There is a five-way switch. The knobs are a Master Volume, a Master Tone, and a Blender knob that mixes in the neck pickup.  I find this wiring more useful and easier than the stock strat wiring (which I honestly have never understood who that was intended for).
There is a slight ding in the body, but otherwise it looks and works great.  The paint was originally Olympic White, but because I believe they used nitrocellulose the color has become slightly more of a cream (which works well with the walnut pickguard.)
I have decided I am more of a Telecaster person after years of playing different styles of guitar, so it is time to let someone else have a chance with this one.

items.ai_notes: [Viking Model F-1 2" Deluge Valve] Industrial fire suppression component. Extremely niche, very slow moving item.
items.description:
The Viking Model F-1 Deluge Valve is a quick opening, differential diaphragm, flood valve with one moving mechanism. The Deluge Valve is used to control water flow in Deluge and Pre-action sprinkler systems. The valve is held closed by system water pressure trapped in the priming chamber, keeping the outlet chamber and system piping dry. In fire conditions, when the releasing system operates, pressure is released from the priming chamber. The Deluge Valve clapper opens to allow water to flow into the system piping.

items.title: Black and Decker 10" bandsaw.    Modified for 240 volts
items.ai_notes: [Black and Decker 10" bandsaw] Modified with a different motor and plug; tracking can be tricky.
items.description:
Up for sale is a tinkerers dream.   I bought this saw with the idea of re sawing wood for my lathe work.  It had a 1/5 hp motor as is usual with these tools.   Way under powered.  So I installed a 1/3 hp condenser motor from a A/C condenser.  So much better.   But it was 240 volts.  A small issue so I installed a long extension cord that plugged in to my welding outlet.   Or a drier outlet also works  fine.
So it uses a 56 1/8" blade.  Saws fine but being 3 wheels, can be a bit tricky on tracking and tension.  Included is extension cord, three blades,  miter gage and the old motor as it still works fine.
I purchased a vintage Delta 10" cast iron band saw to replace it.
If needed and you bring a drier plug with you, I can replace the welder plug with that one.  You can,  however, replace the motor with the old one, but it is just a dog on sawing, so just saying......

items.title: Vintage Heathkit AS-101 / Altec Lansing Valencia-Style Speakers
items.ai_notes: [Heathkit AS-101 Speakers] High-end vintage audio equipment; requires a specific audiophile buyer.
items.description:
For sale is a pair of vintage Heathkit AS-101 speakers, built by the owner in 1972. These are the desirable Heathkit version of the classic Altec Lansing Valencia-style speaker, using Altec Lansing components and drivers clearly marked Altec Lansing.
The Altec Lansing Valencia is one of the classic home hi-fi speakers from the golden age of American audio. It is closely related to Altec’s legendary Voice of the Theatre speaker line, which was originally designed for powerful, clear, highly efficient theater sound. The Valencia brought much of that same horn-loaded Altec character into a furniture-grade home speaker system suitable for serious home listening.
These Heathkit AS-101 speakers deliver the classic Altec sound: open, dynamic, efficient, and very natural. They produce a large, room-filling soundstage with excellent vocal presence, strong center imaging, and a wide sense of space. Music sounds lively and effortless, especially with jazz, vocals, acoustic music, classic rock, orchestral music, and tube or solid-state amplification.
Details:
Pair of vintage Heathkit AS-101 speakers
Altec Lansing Valencia-style design
Built by the owner in 1972
Altec Lansing drivers clearly marked
8 ohm speakers
Crossovers rebuilt in 2025
Cabinets refinished in 2010
Classic horn-loaded Altec sound
Large, open soundstage
Clear vocals and strong dynamics
Excellent choice for a vintage audio system or dedicated listening room
Speakers: Altec Lansing 15 woofer, 10-1/2 pound magnet assembly.  High frequency driver, 13 ounce Alnico V magnet with 800 sectoral horn.
The rebuilt crossovers are a major plus, since crossover age is one of the most common concerns with vintage speakers from this era. The cabinets were refinished in 2010 and present well.
These are serious vintage speakers for someone who understands Altec Lansing, Heathkit AS-101, Valencia-style speakers, or Voice of the Theatre heritage.
Local pickup only. Buyer should bring proper help and a suitable vehicle, as these are large and heavy speakers.  The speakers weigh 101 pounds each.

Contraband 7419 41" loop resistance bands have a variety of uses but are mainly used for warmup, stretching, pull up assistance, bodybuilding, powerlifting, and strongman exercises. We offer a wide range of tensions to handle all kinds of applications.
Intended Use:
We suggest using the lighter bands like ORANGE PURPLE, and YELLOW to stretch and do workouts at home, when traveling, or at the gym. These bands are the most versatile for workouts so we like to suggest purchasing these first if you need a resistance band to help with arms, shoulders, legs, back, and other exercises. The RED band is good for band assisted squats as well as a good starting point for an assisted pullup band, it might be too heavy for stretching or any shoulder or arm work though. BLUE, GREEN, and BLACK are reserved for special purposes, they are the heaviest tension. Just make sure you have a purpose and tried lighter bands before going with one of these.
Materials: Contraband Sports resistance bands are made from a continuous 100% natural latex.
Material Fit: Adjustable with increased tension when stretched
Material Strength: Recommended max tension is suggested on the resistance chart, we suggest stretching the bands no more than 1.5x the unstretched length. If you are unsure, please reach out for support before purchasing so someone can help you choose the best tension for your needs.
Care Instructions: Resistance bands can be cleaned with a damp cloth only, never soak in water or wash with abrasive cleaners.

Ruck Plates are compact and fit seamlessly in the Rucker and Ruck Plate Carrier for superior stability. Made in the USA to exacting standards of quality and craftsmanship, GORUCK Ruck Plates represent the very best of American manufacturing.
Break strength of approximately 90,000 lbs
Powder coated matte black (rust resistant)
Ergonomic, rounded edges and handle openings

Workout without a ruck

Primary Material: Powder Coated Ductile Iron Ore
10LB Dimensions: 9" x 11.5" x 0.52"

30LB (Standard) Dimensions: 9" x 11.5" x 1.38"
30LB (Long) Dimensions: 9.5" x 15" x 0.94"
45LB Dimensions: 9.5" x 15" x 1.38"
Made in the USA (except 10lbs)
Rucksack Compatibility
Our standard of compatibility is that Ruck Plates will be stable and secure in your Ruck with minimal shifting.
If you have a Ruck Plate Carrier, we recommend the shorter (Standard) Ruck Plates -  10LB, 20LB or 30LB.
The 20L and 25L Rucker feature an additional pocket to securely fit a 45LB Ruck Plate, which can be paired with a 20LB or 30LB Ruck Plate for up to 75 lbs of total weight.
If you have a GR1, we recommend the Standard Ruck Plate -  30LB.
45LB Ruck Plates only strap in securely to the 20L/25L Rucker and Long Ruck Plate Carrier, however they will fit into the interior elastic pocket of the GR1 (suitable for upright weighted rucking, but not ruck PT aka burpees and bear crawls).
WHEN IN DOUBT
Start With 20#
The relationship between your body, the weight, and the rucksack will determine your level of comfort on the move. Our recommendation for most people is to start with 20 lbs of weight for rucking, progress in increments of ~10 lbs, and ultimately max out at 1/3 of your bodyweight. It’s more important to keep proper form while rucking than to have more weight.

items.ai_product: Antique UPRR train track level inclinometer
items.title: Antique UPRR train track level inclinometer Union Pacific Rail Road rr
items.ai_notes: [Antique UPRR train track level inclinometer] Seller did not provide a price; highly specialized historical railroad item.
items.description:
This is a very cool vintage railroad level for checking the grade or pitch on the train tracks as they were laid.
Other inclinometers that I have had were fancy models and in great condition and I assume they were gently used by an inspector.
This one has been well used although still in great shape. The condition makes me imagine that it was carried and used as the tracks were laid.
It’s marked UPRR in two places. It’s my understanding that Union Pacific used the UPRR designation until they were done building the Transcontinental Railroad in the mid/late 1800s so this is a very old piece of history. They then changed the name to Union Pacific Railway and used the UPR designation.
It’s also marked with what looks like EV. 6- 66 and the brass level bubble is marked Empire 58”R
It measures 62 1/2” long and the brass elevation ruler is graduated up to 7”
This is an awesome piece of railroading and American history and will make a very nice addition to your collection.
If you know of a nice train museum please let me know or show them this ad and have them contact me.
Thanks

items.title: Infinity Composition Prelude P-FR loudspeaker -Pair
items.description:
Actual photos
In Excellent condition
Rare and Vintage Infinity Composition Prelude P-FR loudspeaker ....  Used in an excellent condition been stored in it's original boxes and packing. See Photos
Here a review from the web:
I can't think of two products at further ends of the audio spectrum than a single-ended triode tubed amplifier and a mass-market Home Theater loudspeaker. Single-ended tubed amplifiers are about reproducing subtlety, delicacy, nuance, and communicating the music's inner essence. Conversely, a Home Theater loudspeaker system—particularly one made by a mass-market manufacturer—would appear to put the emphasis on booming bass and reproducing shotgun blasts, with little regard for musical refinement.
What a bizarre marriage it was, then, to pair the new Infinity Composition Prelude P-FR loudspeakers with the Cary Audio Design CAD-300SEI 11W single-ended triode amplifier (reviewed elsewhere in this issue). This combination didn't happen by accident; as you'll see, these apparently disparate products are a match made in heaven.
I discovered the Infinity Preludes while surveying Home Theater loudspeaker systems for the upcoming second issue of the Stereophile Guide to Home Theater. In addition to evaluating the loudspeaker systems under review with video soundtracks, I assessed their musical qualities—or lack thereof. The Preludes were such a musical standout that I rescued them from the Home Theater room (where they had been powered by mass-market receivers and fed with a laserdisc source) and gave them a new lease on life in the larger music room, with reference-quality source and amplification components. The Preludes' extraordinary musical performance and unique design compelled me to tell you about how they performed in an audiophile-quality two-channel playback system.
Moreover, the Preludes, with their astounding 96dB sensitivity (2.83V/1m) and integral powered woofer, seemed an ideal load for a single-ended amplifier such as the Cary CAD-300SEI integrated amplifier. At $3395, the CAD-300SEI is also a good price match for the $3000/pair Composition Prelude P-FR.
So that's the story of how my listening room ended up home to the two most disparate products imaginable.
Description The Infinity Prelude represents a bold new approach to loudspeaker design. Created by Laurie Fincham (formerly of KEF) and his protégé Andrew Jones (also once with KEF), the Prelude is the culmination of an 18-month–long, ground-up development effort. Every driver and component in the Prelude was designed from scratch specifically for this product, with some design aspects pushing the envelope of what is possible in loudspeaker technology.
The Prelude was designed to combine simplicity of use, elegance, and good video soundtrack reproduction in a Home Theater loudspeaker system. Infinity has more than met those goals (see my review in the Stereophile Guide to Home Theater); but, perhaps more importantly, they created a loudspeaker that provided audiophile-quality musical performance at an affordable price.
The entire Composition Home Theater package consists of left and right loudspeakers with integral powered woofers (the Prelude Full Range, or P-FR), a center-channel speaker (the Prelude Center Channel, or P-CC, footnote 1), and a pair of surrounds (the Prelude Quadrapole Surrounds, or P-QPS). These components are available separately or as a $4448 package. I'll just consider the $3000/pair P-FR left and right loudspeakers in this review.
The P-FR looks unusual, to say the least. The narrow but deep lower enclosure holds a side-loaded 12" woofer. A tall column containing the midrange and treble drivers rises from the woofer enclosure, making the column look a little like a stovepipe. A grille wraps partially around the column, covering the drivers without adding a diffraction-producing obstruction. With a width of only 7.5" at its widest point, the Prelude presents a low profile in the listening room. Nonetheless, the Prelude's sleek, rounded contours and charcoal-gray color make a bold aesthetic statement. It's difficult to overstate the Prelude's elegant and beautiful visual design—"wow" is often the response of visitors upon seeing it.
The enclosure is supported by feet that protrude from the woofer-cabinet edges. You can thread four smooth, flat glides into the feet to make the Prelude moveable, or insert spikes (supplied) for more permanent installations. Switches on the enclosure's bottom rear panel adjust bass level in three increments, change the grounding scheme, and set the Prelude into automatic shutoff mode when no input signal is detected within 10 minutes.
A built-in amplifier drives the system's 12" woofer; you simply connect a pair of loudspeaker cables to the single pair of five-way binding posts. Because of this design, whatever amplifier is driving the Prelude needs power only the midrange and tweeter column. The amplifier is thus relieved of the burden of driving a large amount of current through the woofer's voice-coil. This is one reason why the Prelude is such an appealing load for low-powered tubed amplifiers.
High sensitivity The main reason I acquired an 11Wpc single-ended tubed amplifier to drive the Prelude was, however, the speaker's extraordinarily high sensitivity. With its 96dB rating, the Prelude will play as loudly with the 11W Cary 300SEI as an 87dB-sensitive loudspeaker will play with 88W.
This high sensitivity was achieved with several techniques. First, by using so many drivers (eight per enclosure), the overall radiating area was increased. Moreover, the four-way design allows each driver to be operated over a narrow passband, one where the driver is most sensitive. Second, the drivers represent a groundbreaking, one-year research effort into making a more efficient motor structure. According to Laurie Fincham, only about 25% of a conventional driver's magnetic energy gets into the voice-coil gap. The motor structure developed for the Prelude focuses the magnetic field so that 75% of the magnetic flux gets into the gap. When the voice-coil sits in a stronger magnetic field, it takes less current flow through the voice-coil to pull the voice-coil back and forth, and with it, the cone. Consequently, more of the amplifier power goes to producing sound, and less power is wasted heating the voice-coil.
Surprisingly, the Prelude's single-dome tweeter can keep up with six highly sensitive midrange drivers and a powered woofer. In fact, the tweeter is actually more sensitive than are the other drivers; it's padded down to match the other drivers' output levels. The tweeter uses a shielded Neodymium Iron Boron magnet structure, and is horn-loaded by an "elliptical waveguide" molded into the front baffle. The waveguide increases the tweeter's sensitivity, allows a lower crossover point, and controls the dispersion.
Inside the Prelude Each midrange column contains seven drivers in a line array: four 5.25" lower-midrange units, two 4" upper-midrange drivers, and one 1" soft-dome tweeter in the middle of the column. The Prelude is thus a four-way loudspeaker (including the single 12" woofer). The lower-midrange units use stiffened paper cones (plastic was too heavy to achieve the sensitivity goal), and the upper-midrange diaphragms are made from polypropylene. Crossover frequencies are 110Hz, 350Hz, and 3kHz, with varying slopes. The 20-liter column is high-pass–filtered at 110Hz with a fourth-order slope, and the woofer is high-pass–filtered at 15Hz with a first-order slope. Two small ports at each end of the column provide reflex-loading of the midrange drivers.
Although the column contains seven drivers, it's barely wider than the 5.25" lower-midrange units. This narrow profile confers the advantages of low diffraction, wide dispersion, and excellent imaging; it's no coincidence that minimonitors and other narrow-baffle designs disappear more easily into the soundstage than do large boxes.
The column is made from 3/16" extruded aluminum with a steel baffle. The unusual rounded back discourages the formation of standing waves and makes the enclosure less resonant. A charcoal-gray paint finishes the column.
An 18-liter sealed woofer enclosure houses the Prelude's side-firing 12" drive-unit. The woofer features a massive, 70-oz magnet in a diecast frame that uses the same focused field structure as that used in the midrange drivers and tweeter. The cone material is Infinity's IMG (Injection Molded Graphite), a blend of damped polypropylene and graphite fibers. IMG, used in Infinity's IRS Beta and Epsilon woofers, reportedly provides high rigidity, low mass, and high output without distortion.
Loading a 12" woofer in such a small enclosure puts the resonant frequency very high—in this case, 85Hz. To extend the bass response, the woofer's integral power amplifier is equalized to provide flat response (the system is down 2dB at 35Hz, $*–6dB at 25Hz). The woofer amplifier power isn't specified, but the Preludes each draw a maximum of 300W from the AC outlet [meaning the woofer amplifier probably produces around 100W—Ed.].
The Prelude is a bold effort that rethinks some of the accepted wisdom of loudspeaker design and aesthetics. This was clearly a pioneering design effort that attempted to break free from the traditional loudspeaker paradigms. Moreover, the execution was first-rate—the build quality and finish detail are superb.
Listening In the following description of the Prelude's sound, you won't find any qualifications such as "The Preludes were superb for a Home Theater loudspeaker." Once the Preludes were moved to my music room, I judged them by the highest audiophile standards.
First, the Prelude had an exceptionally smooth, uncolored sound. Its lack of bass bloat and refined—even polite—treble produced a sophisticated, understated sound. This wasn't a loudspeaker that called attention to itself; instead, the Prelude got out of the music's way and reproduced the signal with very little editorial interjection. The Prelude made the music rather than the loudspeakers the center of attention.
The Prelude's treble was clean and detailed, yet not aggressive or etched. It struck a perfect balance between treble resolution and smoothness. The result was an ability to hear lots of fine musical detail without listening fatigue or feeling that my ears wanted to close. The treble refinement and lack of etch seemed to invite me into the music rather than keep me at arm's length. In addition to being well-balanced with the rest of the spectrum, the Prelude's treble lacked grain or metallic brittleness. Cymbals had just the right degree of sheen and air, and weren't overlaid with the "spray can" white-noise–like sound produced by some tweeters. Similarly, vocal sibilance was less spitty and intrusive than I've heard from many loudspeakers. In this regard, the Prelude's treble balance and cleanliness approached the performance of ribbon drivers.
Some listeners may, however, find the Prelude's treble too polite, particularly when driving them with smooth-sounding tubed amplifiers. Fortunately, you can simply toe-in the Prelude slightly for a brighter presentation and increased sense of immediacy. I did all my auditioning either with no toe-in (with the ARC VT150s) or just a little toe-in (with the Cary CAD-300SEI), which ameliorated the Cary amplifier's lack of top-octave air. That's another reason why the Prelude is ideal for single-ended tubed amplifiers: you can dial-in nearly any treble balance you want to compensate for tubed amplifiers' sometimes rolled-off trebles.
This smooth and refined treble was matched to a remarkably uncolored midband. Vocals had an open and unfettered quality that made them seem to exist completely outside the loudspeakers. There was no trace of nasality, congestion, honk, or a hooty quality. In addition to the lack of midband coloration, the Prelude had a wonderful transparency that allowed me to hear deep into the soundstage. The speaker was highly resolving of midrange detail, easily revealing the differences between digital interconnects, for example.
Although the Prelude was highly resolving of the signal fed it, they were never etched, analytical, or "ruthlessly revealing." Instead, the detail was presented in a natural, gentle way that produced a tremendous sense of musical ease and refinement.
When auditioning the Prelude as a Home Theater loudspeaker, I was struck by how smooth the bass sounded. Most Home Theater loudspeakers have a sluggish boom in the lower bass and a lack of articulation in the midbass. Not the Prelude: it had an extraordinarily well-defined and detailed bass, with no hint of boom or bloat.
Acoustic bass was particularly well-served by the Prelude; I could hear detail and nuance often smeared by lesser loudspeakers. Consequently, I found myself greatly enjoying virtuoso bass performances—such as Eddie Gomez's playing on Chick Corea's Friends (Polydor 849 071-2), or his work on Steps Ahead's eponymous debut record (Elektra Musician 60168-2). The Prelude's superb pitch definition and bass articulation were significant factors in my enjoyment of music through it.
Moreover, the bass was seamlessly integrated with the lower midrange. Descending or ascending piano lines that crossed the transition showed no discontinuity or change in character.
The bass was also deep and extended but didn't stretch into the lowermost octaves with the authority I'm used to from the mighty Genesis II.5s. The organ-pedal tones on Timothy Seelig's and the Turtle Creek Chorale and Women's Chorus of Dallas's performance of Rutter's Requiem (Reference RR-57CD) were audible, but the lowermost tones (16Hz) were rolled-off. Nonetheless, the bass extension was deeper than you get from most $3000/pair loudspeakers.
Although the bass was highly articulate, it was on the lean side. Rather than sounding weighty, full, and authoritative, the bass was tight, polite, and refined. I much prefer bass quality to bass quantity, but I would have liked a little more visceral impact and weight from the Prelude. Note, however, that I had the Prelude in a 21' by 18' room, well away from the rear and side walls (and with the woofer-level switch in the "high" position). When placed closer to room boundaries (as I used them in the Home Theater room), the Prelude had greater authority and bass power. Nonetheless, you wouldn't think the Prelude's bass was produced by a big woofer in a reflex enclosure with an underdamped alignment.
The Prelude had a tremendously "quick" bass, with no overhang or smearing. Kickdrum had a "sudden" quality that made it jump out from the presentation and stop as quickly as it started. This quality, coupled with the articulate midbass, combined for a tight, quick, and punchy bottom end.
The rest of the spectrum had similarly impressive dynamics. The snare drum on Michael Ruff's Speaking in Melodies (Sheffield CD-35), for example, had a huge sense of snap and impact—particularly with the ARC VT150s driving the Prelude. The overall dynamic contrast was exceptionally wide: the Prelude could play loudly without congestion and resolve fine detail during quiet passages. Moreover, transients were reproduced with razor-sharp leading edges, with no smearing or dulling of transient detail. Microdynamics were also impressive: listen to drummer Steve Gadd's gentle rim work at the beginning of the aforementioned Friends record, or Ralph Humphry's brushes on Mike Garson's The Oxnard Sessions, Volume Two (Reference RR-53CD).
The icing on the cake was the Prelude's spectacular soundstaging. These loudspeakers threw a precisely defined space before me, with a spatial coherence that was among the best I've heard from any loudspeaker. I could hear precisely where each instrument or voice was in the soundstage, and images were highly focused, tight, and compact, making the presentation sound like a collection of individual instruments in three-dimensional space. There was also a remarkable stability and tangibility to the images, further heightening the impression of instruments before me. Moreover, the Prelude completely disappeared into the soundstage, giving no clue that the sound was being reproduced by two spaced sources. Soundstage depth was also impressive, with both a sense of distance and gradations of layering. The Genesis II.5s had, however, a larger overall soundstage size (width and depth) and presented more bloom and envelopment in the acoustic surrounding the instruments. The Preludes tended to sound smaller and more intimate, with less air at the soundstage edges.
As a result of these specific sonic attributes, I greatly enjoyed music through the Preludes—particularly with the Cary 300SEI. Even with my standards set by the $37,000 combination of the Genesis II.5s and Audio Research electronics, the $6395 Prelude/Cary pair was intensely involving musically.
Although some of the credit goes to the Cary single-ended amplifier, the Preludes were able to communicate the quality of the recordings and source components—and, consequently, communicate the music. In addition, I heard many of the qualities described when auditioning the Prelude with mass-market audio/video receivers for the Stereophile Guide to Home Theater. Although the A/V receivers didn't provide the treble purity and soundstaging I experienced with the tubed electronics, I still heard the Prelude's uncolored tonal balance, excellent bass articulation, and wide dynamics.
With the Cary CAD-300SEI, the Prelude produced completely satisfying playback levels. It's amazing what 11W will do with a 96dB–sensitive loudspeaker (and a powered woofer). This combination was absolutely magical, bringing the purity of single-ended triode amplification to an uncolored, audiophile-quality loudspeaker and providing bass performance that wasn't dependent on the tubed amplifier. The Preludes are the load for low-powered tubed amplifiers.
My only reservation is that you may not be able to audition the Preludes under ideal conditions—they're sold primarily by mass-market stores rather than by specialty-audio retailers. Although they sounded good in the Home Theater system, they didn't really sing until they were optimally set up in the larger music room and driven by topnotch source and amplification components. Once the word gets out about how the Preludes sound with single-ended tubed amplifiers, I suspect more high-end dealers will carry the Preludes. Then you can audition them in their full glory.
Conclusion The Infinity Composition Prelude P-FR loudspeaker is a stunning musical, technical, and aesthetic achievement. Even without its high sensitivity, the Prelude's smooth and uncolored tonal balance, wide dynamic contrast, articulate bass, and wonderful soundstaging would make it a standout. But with its ability to be driven to satisfying levels using an 11W single-ended triode amplifier, the Prelude becomes the loudspeaker for such amplifiers. Indeed, the $6395 Cary CAD-300SEI/Prelude combination was one of the most musical-sounding systems I've heard—regardless of price.
It is difficult to criticize the Prelude at its bargain price of $3000/pair. I've heard high-end loudspeakers costing more than twice the Prelude's price that didn't provide anywhere near this level of musical performance. None$*theless, I found the bass balance a little on the lean side in my large room—a little more weight and authority would have been welcome. In addition, the polite treble contributed to less sense of air, which made the soundstage less expansive than that heard from many loudspeakers.
My descriptions of specific aspects of the Prelude's performance throughout this review don't tell the whole story. What I want to leave you with is how greatly I enjoyed music through the Prelude, particularly with the Cary 300SEI. I experienced many transcendental musical moments with this moderately priced combination.
The Infinity Prelude is worthy of my highest recommendation. In fact, I gave them the ultimate vote of confidence: I bought the review samples.—Robert Harley

items.title: FOUR FLAGS RALLY VINTAGE MOTORCYCLE RIDE! FREE!
items.ai_notes: [Four Flags Rally event] This is an announcement for a motorcycle rally event, not an item for sale.
items.description: The RiverCity Ramblers' TWENTY-FOURTH ANNUAL Four Flags Rally, a real road ride like most owners of vintage motorcycles only daydream about, will start at 9:00 A.M. on SATURDAY, 7/11/2026, at the Harp's Food store (park on the gravel and grass east of the store or in the FAR SOUTHEAST corner of their parking lot) at 1107 South Main Street across from the Casey's General Store on OK Highway 20 just west of downtown Jay, OK. It's GPS coordinates are: latitude: 36* 25' 9"; longitude: -94* 48' 23". You may leave your truck parked there. Casey's sells non-ethanol gas, and please start with your bike full of gas. Riders of all PRE-1990 vintage, street-legal motorcycles of UNDER 501cc (NO EXCEPTIONS, PLEASE) are welcome on this approximately 195-mile one-day tour through four states (OK-KS-MO-AR). This event is designed to be a safe yet challenging ride for medium-size vintage motorcycles. Our ride will include a quick stop at Jim Serage's great Second Kick Cycle Works Museum in Grove, two crossings of Grand Lake, a ride under the bluffs along the Elk River at Noel, MO, and many miles in the foothills of the beautiful Ozark Mountains. We will take a cooldown break - swimming optional - at the Grand Falls of Shoal Creek on the west side of Joplin. We will eat lunch at Van's Steakhouse in Baxter Springs. We need to MAINTAIN 55 MPH for several stretches of U.S. Highways, so this may not be the ideal ride for bikes of under 125cc. Your food and gas should be your only costs for the ride. A sag wagon will be provided to haul tools, gas, water and inop bikes. Everyone who rides the Four Flags Rally will receive a commemorative ride button and a nice 8.5" X 11" color photo of his choice from among vintage motorcycle subjects. To encourage the riding of older, truly vintage bikes, riders of all 1969 or older bikes will receive a 1960s-vintage issue of Cycle World magazine. Several trophies will be awarded, and all riders will be entered into a drawing for nice prizes, which include the book History of Japanese Motorcycles 1945-2007 (the definitive reference source for Japanese bikes), a motorcycle wheel balancer, sound recordings from the 1966 Isle of Man TT races and more. We will have an earlybird drawing for those entered by 8:30 A.M. For more info, call Larry @ 918-2five8-2four00.

items.title: Antique UPRR train track level inclinometer Union Pacific Rail Road rr
items.ai_notes: [Antique UPRR railroad level] Collectible railroad tool; no price provided.
items.description:
This is a very cool vintage railroad level for checking the grade or pitch on the train tracks as they were laid.
Other inclinometers that I have had were fancy models and in great condition and I assume they were gently used by an inspector.
This one has been well used although still in great shape. The condition makes me imagine that it was carried and used as the tracks were laid.
It’s marked UPRR in two places. It’s my understanding that Union Pacific used the UPRR designation until they were done building the Transcontinental Railroad in the mid/late 1800s so this is a very old piece of history. They then changed the name to Union Pacific Railway and used the UPR designation.
It’s also marked with what looks like EV. 6- 66 and the brass level bubble is marked Empire 58”R
It measures 62 1/2” long and the brass elevation ruler is graduated up to 7”
This is an awesome piece of railroading and American history and will make a very nice addition to your collection.
If you know of a nice train museum please let me know or show them this ad and have them contact me.
Thanks

items.title: Rare David Janssen Harry O Novels # 1 # 2 Harry O High Cost of Living
items.description:
Rare
Harry O #1 by Lee Hays
First novel "Harry O #1," was published in 1975 and is the first of two novels for the popular
70s Private Detective TV show.
The book follows Harry Orwell, a retired San Diego PD officer, as he is hired by Mary Alice Kimberly
to protect her from death threats from her ex-husband.
The story unfolds as Harry becomes embroiled in a complex case involving a private eye's body and
the smuggling of heroin.
Very good novel that stays true to the original series (it's an original story not a novelization of an
existing episode).
Fans of the show will definitely enjoy this book. Set in the early days of the series when Harry was
still in San Diego and dealing with his friend police Lt. Manny Quinlan.
Told in the first person it really catches the world weary "voice" of Harry Orwell as originally
portrayed by David Janssen.
"Harry O: The High Cost of Living," #2 blend of mystery and adventure, set against the backdrop of
the 70s Private Detective TV show.
The novels follow the adventures of Harry Orwell, a retired San Diego PD officer who becomes a
private investigator. The series has been praised for its engaging storytelling and has become a
favorite among fans of the original TV show.
RARE!

items.title: Uranium Glass Vintage Anchor Hocking Block Optic Set
items.description:
This matching vintage green glass set includes a footed covered candy dish, creamer, and open sugar bowl in the classic Block Optic pattern.
The set has the bold geometric look that makes Depression glass so recognizable, and all three pieces glow brightly under UV light, making them especially appealing for uranium glass collectors and display.
Produced by Hocking Glass during the early Depression era, these pressed glass pieces are a strong example of American glassware from that period. The design is both decorative and functional, with a raised paneled pattern, footed bases, and a rich green color that stands out nicely whether displayed in normal light or under blacklight.
All three pieces are vintage originals and are unmarked, which is typical for many examples from this era. Condition is good overall with expected wear from age and use. The open sugar bowl has a chip on one handle, which is shown in the photos. Please look over all pictures carefully for full condition details.
